column1: # guard-budget.tsv — the guard/test shell line-count ceiling (#641).
# ONE data row: ceiling <TAB> as_of <TAB> reason.
#   ceiling  Total lines across every file scripts/check-guard-budget.sh classifies as
#            guard/test shell (its own header documents the classification exactly).
#   as_of    ISO date the ceiling was last set.
#   reason   Empty unless this row RAISES the ceiling over its previous committed value — then
#            it names why. scripts/check-guard-budget.sh reds a raise carrying no reason.
# The ratchet only goes down: nothing here auto-lowers the number on a merge (that would need
# CI to commit to main unsupervised, which this repo grants no workflow the permissions for —
# docs/plans/second-shift-641-lean.md's Known trades). Instead the check prints an advisory
# whenever the tree measures under the committed ceiling, naming the lower value so an operator
# can ratchet it down as a normal, reviewed edit. A PR that adds guard mass without deleting at
# least as much pushes the measured total over this row's ceiling and reds.
# Raising the ceiling is a deliberate, reviewed edit: bump the number, stamp today's date, and
# say why in the reason column — the escape hatch for a genuinely new guard, priced so it is
# visible at review rather than absorbed silently.
